claims.text: SPD followed by controlled aging creates a heterogeneous, nanorefined microstructure in HEAs.
The proposed dual processing route simultaneously improves strength, ductility, Young's modulus, and fracture resistance.
Severe plastic deformation refines the grains of the HEA.
Controlled thermal aging induces nanoscale precipitate formation.
Appropriate control of SPD strain rate, temperature, and total strain avoids excessive damage.
Appropriate control of aging temperature and time produces nanoscale phases without coarsening.
The proposed route produces ultrafine grains with uniformly dispersed nanoscale precipitates.
Interfaces associated with the ultrafine grains and precipitates impede dislocation motion while permitting strain accommodation.
Grain-boundary strengthening from the refined grain structure increases strength.
The refined grain structure and elastically stiff interfaces increase Young's modulus.
Nanoscale precipitates impede dislocation propagation and increase strength without compromising ductility.
The combined ultrafine-grain and nanoprecipitate structure deflects or arrests cracks and thereby improves fracture toughness.
Relative to conventionally cast and homogenized HEAs, the dual-processed material will exhibit a 15–20% improvement in yield strength.
The dual-processed material will exhibit elongation greater than 10%.
The dual-processed material will have a higher Young's modulus and fracture toughness than the conventionally processed baseline.
Conventionally cast and homogenized HEAs typically exhibit inferior combinations of strength and ductility.
The route may fail when SPD creates excessive defects, the composition cannot form beneficial precipitates, or processing parameters are not optimized.
Direct experimental evidence for this specific HEA process–property relationship is currently limited.
